title: capacity-surge-simulation-notes-apac-eu-weekly
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note capturing the latest round of discrete surge simulations run against cluster pools in APAC and EU for July week-of-2026-07-18. Goal: evaluate microburst impact on slot fragmentation, p95 tail latency, and failover behavior when dedicated capacity is constrained and routing policy falls back to shared pools. This doc combines raw dashboard exports, quick sanity checks, and recommended mitigations to iterate on the production playbook.

Dataset and inputs used:
- Window: 2026-07-12 to 2026-07-22 (10 days), sampled at 1-minute resolution from the telemetry ingestion pipeline.
- Sources: telemetry-v2:gpu_pool_metrics, request-router:route_events, kv-cache:hit_stats.
- Simulation driver: surge-sim-v3 (local runner) using replay of 3 real customer traces (trace ids: trace-239, trace-301, trace-422) with injected burst multipliers [1.5x, 3x, 6x].
- Pools tested: apac-gpu-pool-2 (A100p), eu-gpu-pool-3 (H100), shared-gpu-fallback-eu.
- Key metrics exported from dashboards: avg_slot_util, active_slots, idle_slots_frag, p50_token_latency_ms, p95_token_latency_ms, microburst_count (>90% util for >= 10s).

Quick export snapshot (sample rows from dashboard export):
Date | Cluster | Pool | avg_slot_util | active_slots | idle_slots_frag | p95_token_latency_ms | microburst_count
2026-07-19 | apac-cluster-7 | apac-gpu-pool-2 | 0.68 | 124 | 12 | 46 | 7
2026-07-19 | eu-cluster-4   | eu-gpu-pool-3   | 0.74 | 96  | 18 | 58 | 11
2026-07-20 | eu-cluster-4   | shared-gpu-fallback-eu | 0.54 | 42 | 5 | 62 | 3

Topline observations (what jumped out):
- Microbursts correlate strongly with sudden decreases in idle_slots_frag when burst multiplier >= 3x. In eu-gpu-pool-3, we saw fragmentation collisions (many small allocations) that prevented efficient colocations, pushing logical slot demand into shared pools.
- p95 token latency increased by ~20–30ms during 3x surges and ~60–110ms during 6x surges. Tail spikes are more pronounced in H100 pool under mixed-length sequences (seq len variance > 4x).
- Routing fallback worked but exposed cold-warm handoff that generated elevated p50 latencies for the first 30s of heavy spillover (observed in shared-gpu-fallback-eu).
- Cache warming (kv-cache) reduced token generation p95 by ~12% if warm-hit rate >= 0.6 at the time of surge; this effect is most visible in APAC traces with repeated prefixes.

Diagnostics and checks performed:
- Replayed same trace with quantization profiles toggled (int8 vs bf16). Int8 runs show slightly higher microburst_count but lower average slot footprint enabling more colocations.
- Ran slot coalescing experiment (temp flag coalesce_agg=on) — reduced idle_slots_frag by ~9% in apac pool but introduced 5–8ms additional scheduling overhead; net p95 improved in 3x sim but worsened slightly in 6x sim.
- Verified eviction logs to ensure no customer-level preemption events were misattributed — none found in these runs.

Actionable recommendations (short-term):
1) Enable lightweight slot coalescing for pools with avg utilization > 0.6 and seq-length-variance < 3. Reason: reduces fragmentation without overly penalizing scheduler overhead. Flag/rollout: canary 20% of apac-gpu-pool-2.
2) Update routing policy low-latency-fallback: when spillover to shared pool occurs, hold a grace lane (warm handoff) by pre-warming 2 reserved slots per customer when predicted traffic spike probability > 0.25. This reduces first-30s p50 penalty.
3) Implement a microburst detector that increases short-lived burst-burst weight rather than full capacity reallocation. Trigger thresholds: sustained util > 0.9 for >= 10s AND predicted incoming QPS delta >= 2x.
4) Short-term capacity booking: schedule an APAC A100 bump ( +8 slots) for the 72-hour window following any large marketing campaign; tracked via JIRA-OPS-1429.

Longer-term ideas (backlog):
- Scheduler: move from fixed slice durations to adaptive slice sizing tied to observed sequence-length distributions (helps H100 under mixed sequences).
- Auto-quantization policy by workload: try mixed-precision per-request; fall back gracefully based on quality-estimation hook.
- Predictive pre-warm model: cheap client-side signal + server-side probability estimator to pre-allocate warm contexts for repeat prefixes.

Open questions / things to validate next run:
- Does coalescing negatively impact multi-tenant noisy neighbors when we see adversarial payload shapes? Need a targeted run with synthetic noisy tenants.
- How to parameterize pre-warm grace lanes across enterprise customers vs free-tier? Proposed: entitlement-based default 0–2 lanes.
- Validate whether longer slice sizes amplify microburst tail (initial hypothesis: longer slices allow better batching but increase latency on cold start).

Notes on exports and reproducibility:
- Full run artifacts stored: s3://redwood-prod-telemetry/surge-sim/2026-07-19/run-003.tar.gz (contains driver config, raw telemetry export, and instrumentation histograms).
- Basic SQL used for the dashboard export: SELECT minute_ts, cluster, pool, AVG(util) AS avg_slot_util, COUNT(active_slot) AS active_slots, SUM(case when idle_duration<60 then 1 else 0 end) AS idle_slots_frag, PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY token_latency_ms) AS p95_token_latency_ms FROM telemetry_v2.gpu_pool_metrics WHERE minute_ts BETWEEN '2026-07-12' AND '2026-07-22' AND cluster IN ('apac-cluster-7','eu-cluster-4') GROUP BY minute_ts, cluster, pool;
- Visualization notes: the key signal to plot is idle_slots_frag (as a stacked area) overlaid with microburst_count (bar) and routed_spillover_percent (line).

Immediate next steps / owner map:
- Priya: drive canary for slot coalescing flag in apac-gpu-pool-2 (canary config + dashboard). Deadline: 2026-07-28.
- Marco: implement microburst detector prototype in local driver (instrumentation + alert). Deadline: 2026-07-26.
- Chen: update routing fallback test harness to simulate warm-handoff lanes & measure p50 impact. Deadline: 2026-07-25.
- Ava: coordinate capacity booking JIRA and communicate with sales for potential committed capacity events. Deadline: 2026-07-22 (in-flight).

Rough risk/impact scoring (1–5):
- Slot coalescing: impact 4, risk 2 (low to medium)
- Warm-handoff lanes: impact 3, risk 3 (routing complexity)
- Microburst detector: impact 4, risk 2 (instrumentation required)

Quick retro on the simulation mechanics (notes to self):
- The synthetic multiplier approach is helpful for stress testing but tends to amplify rare combination states that are unlikely in normal traffic; prioritize runs that replay observed traces with small multiplier steps (1.2x, 1.5x, 2x) before doing 6x extremes.
- Ensure all runs attach the KV cache snapshots — missing cache state makes p95 numbers noisy.

Appendix (links to dashboards / raw tables):
- Dashboard (temp export): https://dashboards.redwood/internal/inf/surge-sim/2026-07-19
- Raw table export location: s3://redwood-data-exports/infrastructure/surge-sim/2026-07-19/table-export.csv
- Trace ids and short notes: trace-239 (product search heavy, short seqs), trace-301 (chatty assistant long-form), trace-422 (bursting telemetry ingestion).

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally a working document — please add comments inline or push PRs to the surge-sim-runbook confluence page. We will convert to a formal playbook if the canary shows net positive outcomes.
